Critical minerals have become one of the most important topics in international trade. As demand continues to grow for electric vehicles, renewable energy, semiconductors, aerospace, and advanced manufacturing, countries are working to secure reliable supplies of the raw materials that make these technologies possible. Today, China plays a leading role in the mining, processing, and refining of many critical minerals, including rare earth elements, graphite, antimony, and tungsten. Over many years, China invested in processing facilities, developed long-term relationships with mining companies around the world, and built an extensive supply chain that serves manufacturers across multiple industries. As a result, changes in China’s production or export policies can have a significant impact on global markets.

Critical minerals underpin industries worth trillions of dollars, and import dependence puts key sectors at risk.”

Source: U.S. Department of the Interior / USGS 
Publication: 2025 List of Critical Minerals
Date: November 14, 2025

For businesses in the United States, these developments create both challenges and opportunities. Manufacturers that rely on imported critical minerals may face supply disruptions, longer delivery times, higher costs, or greater price volatility when global supply becomes tighter. Companies producing batteries, semiconductors, renewable energy equipment, industrial machinery, electronics, and defense-related products all depend on a stable supply of these materials. At the same time, the U.S. Government has responded by encouraging domestic mining, expanding mineral processing, investing in recycling, supporting strategic stockpiles, and strengthening partnerships with allied countries. These efforts are designed to diversify supply sources, reduce dependence on any single country, and build a more resilient critical minerals supply chain for the future.

China’s long-term investment in critical minerals demonstrates that strong supply chains are built over many years through strategic planning, infrastructure, processing capacity, and international partnerships. Rebuilding or expanding supply chains elsewhere will also require time, investment, and cooperation between governments and private industry. For companies operating in today’s global market, the most effective strategy is often to diversify sourcing, develop trusted supplier relationships, and maintain greater visibility across the entire supply chain. Organizations that plan ahead and build resilient procurement strategies are generally better prepared to manage market uncertainty and respond to future changes in global trade.

Did You Know?

  • Higher procurement risk – Manufacturers may need to qualify multiple suppliers instead of relying on a single source.
  • Greater price volatility – Export restrictions or supply disruptions can lead to sudden increases in raw material costs.
  • Longer planning cycles – Companies may hold more inventory or negotiate longer-term supply agreements to reduce risk.
  • Supply chain diversification – Businesses are increasingly sourcing from multiple countries rather than a single market.
  • Increased investment – U.S. companies are investing in domestic mining, refining, recycling, and processing to strengthen long-term supply security.
  • Strategic partnerships – Governments and private companies are expanding cooperation with trusted partners in regions such as Australia, Canada, Southeast Asia, and other allied countries to improve supply chain resilience.

At Wohnen, we believe informed decisions begin with reliable market intelligence. By monitoring global developments, maintaining trusted international partnerships, and supporting responsible sourcing, we help our customers build stronger, more resilient critical mineral supply chains for long-term success.”

title.rendered: Critical Mineral Spotlight: Rare Earth Elements

content.rendered:
Rare Earth Elements, often called REEs, are a group of 17 minerals that play an important role in many of today’s most advanced technologies. Although they are called “rare,” many of these elements are found in the Earth’s crust. The challenge is that they are not often found in large concentrations that are economical to mine and process. Rare earth elements are essential because they have unique magnetic, electrical, and chemical properties that are difficult to replace with other materials. Without them, many of the technologies we rely on every day would not perform as efficiently or, in some cases, would not be possible at all.

Rare earth elements are indispensable for permanent magnets used in wind turbines and electric vehicles.”

Source: International Energy Agency (IEA)
Publication: Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2024 – Analysis – IEA 
Date: May 2024
Organization: International Energy Agency (IEA)

Rare earth elements are used in a wide range of products and industries. Neodymium and praseodymium are used to produce powerful permanent magnets found in electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, robotics, smartphones, computer hard drives, and medical imaging equipment. Dysprosium and terbium help these magnets continue to perform under high temperatures, making them suitable for demanding industrial and transportation applications. Europium, yttrium, and terbium are used in LED lighting, television displays, and computer screens to produce bright and accurate colors. Other rare earth elements are used in satellites, radar systems, aerospace technologies, precision manufacturing, industrial lasers, and advanced defense equipment. As industries continue to adopt cleaner energy and smarter technologies, the demand for rare earth elements is expected to grow for many years to come.

At Wohnen, we understand that rare earth elements are more than valuable minerals—they are the foundation of many modern technologies that support everyday life and future innovation. Securing a dependable supply requires responsible sourcing, strong international partnerships, careful quality management, and reliable logistics. We work closely with trusted partners throughout the supply chain to help customers gain access to high-quality critical minerals while supporting transparency, consistency, and long-term supply security.

Our commitment is to deliver responsibly sourced critical minerals with the trust, reliability, and transparency that customers expect from a long-term supply chain partner. “

Did You Know?

A modern electric vehicle can use more than one kilogram of rare earth elements in its permanent magnet motor, while a single large offshore wind turbine may require hundreds of kilograms of rare earth magnets to generate clean electricity. These unique materials help make renewable energy technologies more efficient, reliable, and powerful.

title.rendered: CEO Message: Antimony is our Business

content.rendered:
“Since founding Wohnen in 1993, our journey has always been guided by one principle—building trusted partnerships that connect opportunities across international markets. We began as an international trading house serving customers throughout Asia and beyond. Over the years, we expanded into specialized technology through our Electronic Warfare business unit while strengthening our capabilities in international trade, logistics, financing, compliance, and relationship management. In 2023, we entered a new chapter by making critical minerals—particularly antimony—the primary focus of our international trading business. We recognized that industries around the world were entering a period where secure access to critical minerals would become just as important as price and product quality. Our experience in global trade positioned us to help customers navigate this rapidly changing market with confidence.

Critical minerals are more than commodities—they are the foundation of tomorrow’s industries. Our responsibility is to build trusted partnerships that deliver certainty in an uncertain world.”

— Boonsom Nimaramwang, Founder & Chief Executive Officer

The second half of 2025 marked an important milestone in our journey. Working alongside established international trading partners, Wohnen participated in supplying large-scale antimony metal ingots into Europe as part of the industrial supply chain supporting NATO member countries. That experience reinforced our belief that success in the critical minerals industry is built on more than simply buying and selling materials. It requires an integrated ecosystem of trusted mining partners, processors, smelters, inspection agencies, logistics providers, warehousing operators, financial institutions, and customers working together toward a common goal. Our role is to connect every part of this supply chain—from source to market—while delivering transparency, quality assurance, responsible sourcing, and dependable international logistics that our customers can rely on.

Today, our customers are looking for more than a supplier—they are looking for a trusted long-term partner who understands the global market and can help manage supply chain risk in an increasingly complex world. That is the value Wohnen brings to every relationship. We combine more than three decades of international trading experience with an integrated global network to provide reliable access to commercial-grade antimony and other critical minerals. We believe trust is earned through every shipment, every commitment, and every partnership we build. As global demand for critical minerals continues to grow, our mission remains clear: to connect trusted sources with global markets while creating lasting value for our customers, partners, and the industries we proudly serve.”

With utmost respect,

Boonsom Nimaramwang

Founder & Chief Executive Officer

The European Union (EU) is one of the world’s largest consumers of critical minerals. These materials support many important industries, including renewable energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, electronics, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing. As Europe continues its transition toward a greener and more digital economy, the demand for reliable supplies of critical minerals is expected to increase significantly. Because many of these minerals are imported, the European Union is working to strengthen supply chain resilience by building long-term partnerships with trusted suppliers around the world.

Europe’s access to a secure, diversified, affordable and sustainable supply of critical raw materials is a prerequisite for achieving our green and digital ambitions.”

Source: European Commission
Publication: Critical Raw Materials Act – Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs 
Date: March 16, 2023 (updated implementation information through 2025)
Organization: European Commission

Among the critical minerals receiving greater attention is antimony. The European Union recognizes antimony as a strategic raw material because of its importance in flame-retardant materials, semiconductors, batteries, defense, and other industrial applications. In recent years, supply disruptions and tighter export controls from major producing countries have highlighted the need for more diversified sources of supply. As a result, European manufacturers are seeking reliable international partners that can provide consistent quality, transparent sourcing, and dependable delivery. At the same time, the EU is investing in recycling, mineral processing, and strategic projects to strengthen its long-term supply security while maintaining responsible environmental and social standards.

The European Union has also introduced new policies to improve the resilience of its critical mineral supply chains. Through the Critical Raw Materials Act, the EU aims to increase domestic extraction, expand processing capacity, improve recycling, and diversify imports from trusted international partners. These initiatives are designed to reduce supply risks while supporting Europe’s long-term industrial competitiveness and clean energy ambitions. For companies operating in the global critical minerals industry, these developments present new opportunities to build stronger partnerships and support a more secure and sustainable supply chain.

Wohnen is committed to supporting European customers with responsibly sourced critical minerals, trusted global partnerships, and reliable supply chain solutions that create long-term value.

At Wohnen, we closely monitor developments across the European Union because they influence global demand, sourcing strategies, and international trade. We understand that customers need more than access to materials—they need confidence in the quality, transparency, and reliability of their supply chain. By working with trusted partners and maintaining responsible sourcing practices, Wohnen is committed to helping customers meet the evolving needs of European industries with dependable critical mineral solutions.

Flame retardants help slow the spread of fire and improve safety in many everyday products. They are used in building materials, electrical cables, electronics, textiles, automotive components, and industrial equipment. Their purpose is to reduce fire risks and give people more time to respond during an emergency. Fire safety standards around the world continue to make flame-retardant materials an important part of modern manufacturing.

Its biggest application today is as a flame retardant, which accounted for around half of global usage in 2023.”

Source: Reuters
Article:  Explainer: What is antimony and why is China curbing its exports? | Reuters
Reported by: Reuters Staff, August 16, 2024.

Antimony is one of the key minerals used in many flame-retardant systems. In the form of antimony trioxide, it works together with other flame-retardant materials to improve fire resistance in a wide range of products. As industries continue to grow and safety regulations become more stringent, manufacturers are placing greater importance on securing reliable sources of high-quality raw materials.

Antimony is one of the world’s most important critical minerals, even though many people have never heard of it. It is a naturally occurring element that has been used for hundreds of years and continues to play an essential role in modern industries. Today, antimony is used to improve the performance, strength, and safety of many products that people use every day. It is found in flame-retardant materials, lead-acid batteries, semiconductors, solar panels, specialty glass, electronic components, and industrial alloys. Because there are very few materials that can fully replace antimony in these applications, it has become an increasingly valuable resource for manufacturers around the world. 

Its biggest application today is as a flame retardant, which accounted for around half of global usage in 2023.”

Source: European Commission
Article: Explainer: What is antimony and why is China curbing its exports? | Reuters
Date: August 16, 2024
Author: Reuters Staff

The importance of antimony has grown significantly in recent years as countries focus on strengthening their critical mineral supply chains. Demand has increased from industries such as renewable energy, advanced manufacturing, electronics, and infrastructure. At the same time, governments are recognizing antimony as a strategic mineral because of its importance to economic security and industrial development. Global supply has become tighter due to limited mining capacity, declining ore grades in some producing regions, and export restrictions from major suppliers. These developments have encouraged manufacturers to diversify their sources of supply and build long-term relationships with trusted international partners. As businesses continue to invest in new technologies and modern infrastructure, antimony is expected to remain an important mineral supporting global industrial growth.

At Wohnen, we understand that supplying antimony is about much more than delivering a product. We believe long-term success is built on trust, consistency, and strong partnerships. By combining market knowledge with reliable supply chain management, Wohnen is committed to helping customers navigate the changing critical minerals market with confidence.

Our commitment is to deliver responsibly sourced critical minerals with the trust, reliability, and transparency that customers expect from a long-term supply chain partner.
